description: Both the implementation's own header comment and the spec cite `scripts/disk-cleaner.sh` as an already-established 'mkdir-atomic lock' precedent in this repo, used to justify NOT writing a fresh test/design for the lock mechanism from scratch ('macOS has no flock(1) binary, both those scripts already solve this the same way'). No such file exists anywhere in this repository: `Glob scripts/*.sh` under the repo root returns zero results (no `scripts/` directory exists at all, on this feature branch or on the checked-out main tree). The ONLY actually-existing sibling precedent, `skills/self/claude-p-mainloop.sh`, uses a PIDFILE guard explicitly documented as 'NOT flock' (its own header, lines 7-9) -- a materially different mechanism (a single global pidfile vs. this feature's `mkdir`-based directory lock) than the one claimed to already exist twice over. This is a fabricated code-precedent citation baked into both the implementation comments (which future maintainers will trust) and the spec's own REQ-708 justification text.

corroborating.note: same fabricated dual-precedent claim repeated in the spec's own REQ-708 EARS text.
the only real sibling script uses a pidfile, and its own header explicitly says 'NOT flock' -- a single-file pidfile guard, not an mkdir-atomic directory lock.
